items.title: Joseph Rene Interview, 1960-09-08
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] ...you know, Tump, man, they wouldn't play it now anymore.

ctx.x: Oh yeah, yeah, we played that same amount of air. They ain't much distant to the customers. They ain't much distant to the customer playing than there was then, because it's the most of the same thing. But the honest thing, I never did follow a band after the funeral, you know, lately. But we used to play our main song, all used to play it, Diddy Rambo. Do they play that yet? They don't play that no more. You ever follow a band after the funeral?

Well, the Dukes of Calvonia, they buried a guy down from the Calvonia Club. And they did. But I'd say unless the guy is a real corner guy, you know, Tump, man, they wouldn't play it now anymore. I don't know why.

Oh yeah, well, yes, but it is. Well all the bands used to play it, because most of the fellas, they used to play, they all used to ramble. See? They all would see the good time or you know, a little bit of shit. They'd do something, they would smile some way or another. But all the bands had that customer. They'd ramble until the butcher caught them down. Every band used to play that when the funeral was over. And I don't know if the bands do that now, sometimes lacking the hoops in the table, it didn't go out…
